h1: The 6 Best Easy-to-Use Printers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six easy-to-use home printers compared on setup flow, on-screen guidance, document feeders and ink access.
summary: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the easiest starting point, with a simple wireless setup flow and a clearly labeled cartridge door. The Canon PIXMA TS6520 adds an OLED screen that explains problems, and the TR4720 simplifies scanning with a document feeder. The TS3720 keeps controls to a minimum.
intro: Easy to use is mostly decided in the first ten minutes and the first jam. A printer that connects to Wi-Fi in a few taps but buries its error messages will frustrate you later. Judge setup and troubleshooting separately.

We reviewed eight home printers and ranked six for setup flow, on-screen guidance, controls and how simply they handle everyday jobs. Rankings come from the spec sheets, and we did not time a setup ourselves.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The simplest start for a first-time printer buyer.
products.description:
HP built the DeskJet 4355 around a short wireless setup and a cartridge door that is plainly labeled. It prints, scans and copies in color, ships with a 3-month Instant Ink trial and lands in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks first because two of the most common beginner stumbling blocks, connecting and changing ink, are addressed directly. It lacks the OLED display of the TS6520.

It suits first-time buyers and non-technical households. Its compact body leaves little room for extras like a feeder.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen spells out what is wrong.
products.description:
Canon gives the TS6520 a 1.42-inch OLED that shows plain status messages, plus duplex printing and a built-in copier and scanner. The control panel is easy to read, and the price is in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks second since the display makes troubleshooting less of a guess, but its setup flow is not described as simply as HP's.

It suits buyers who dread error lights. It does not add a document feeder.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want help when something fails.
products.skipIf: You never look at the display.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A document feeder takes the pain out of scanning.
products.description:
The TR4720 stands out for its auto document feeder, which scanning-heavy homes will notice immediately. It also adds mobile printing, wireless and a legacy fax, all in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks third because the feeder simplifies multipage scanning, which none of the higher picks offer, while its day-to-day controls are less guided.

It suits households that scan bills and forms often. The fax feature is a legacy extra most people will ignore.

products.name: Canon TS6420 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Clear button labels and a simple wireless setup flow.
products.description:
Canon's TS6420 prints, scans and copies in color, with a short wireless setup and a button layout where each key is clearly labeled. Expect the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks fourth because it costs a band more than the cheaper Canons without adding a feeder or display.

It suits buyers who prefer physical buttons to touch menus. It is cartridge-based, so ink costs add up.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact single-tray printer with app support.
products.description:
The TS4320 keeps things simple with one paper tray, duplex printing and app-based printing from a phone. A built-in copier and scanner and a 1-year limited warranty come at $50 to $100.

It ranks fifth because it has none of the guidance extras of the TS6520, but it keeps the same duplex and app basics.

It suits people who print the same few things each week.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Stripped down to the basics, with no feeder or fax.
products.description:
Canon's TS3720 is the plain option: a small, inexpensive color printer that scans and copies over wireless, with no document feeder and no fax. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks last because it offers the fewest features, yet that is the point for people who want the fewest buttons.

It suits light users and older relatives. Heavy scanning is better done on the TR4720.

whatMatters.detail: Setup is the connection of the printer to your Wi-Fi and phone. A guided flow saves the worst frustration. Look for a described simple wireless setup, and have your Wi-Fi password ready.
A display explains errors in words instead of blinking lights. That matters during paper jams. A 1.42-inch OLED is small but clear. Check whether the listing names a display.
Labeled physical buttons are faster for simple copy jobs than menus. Fewer buttons also means less to learn. Look at product photos for the control panel.
An auto document feeder pulls pages in one at a time for scanning. Without one you place each page on the glass. If you scan often, the feeder is the real easy-to-use feature.
A clearly labeled cartridge door makes ink changes less intimidating. It is a small detail that reduces mistakes. Look for it in the feature bullets.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A guided wireless setup, labeled ink door and as few settings as possible.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HP DeskJet 4355 lists all three setup helpers; the Canon TS3720 minimizes controls.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want buttons you can read at a glance. The Canon TS6420 labels its layout.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print occasionally. The HP DeskJet 4355 sits in the $50 to $100 band.

faq.q: Do these need a computer to set up?
faq.a: Most can be set up from a phone app over Wi-Fi. The HP DeskJet 4355 describes a simple wireless flow.
Pairing over the wrong Wi-Fi network. Make sure your phone is on the same network as the printer.

faq.q: Is the TR4720 worth it over the TS3720?
faq.a: Yes if you scan. The TR4720 adds an auto document feeder.
Open the labeled access door and follow the prompts. The HP DeskJet 4355 labels the door clearly.

faq.q: How do I keep ink from drying?
faq.a: Print a page every week or two.

faq.q: Can I print from a phone?
faq.a: The TR4720 and TS4320 list mobile printing support.

finalTake: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the easiest printer to live with for most people. The Canon PIXMA TS6520 is the one to buy if on-screen help matters, and the TR4720 is for anyone who scans. The TS3720 is the minimalist choice for light use.
